# `Q-26-2` — Unsupported markdown inside an lmd fragment

> A markdown fragment in an lmd cell contains a node the fragment emitter has no constructor for, such as a footnote definition or a shortcode. The cell is left as written and does not run.

## What this means

A markdown fragment inside an lmd cell is parsed as markdown and rewritten
into `pandoc.*` constructor calls. The fragment contained a kind of node
that this rewriting does not support yet, so the cell was not run and stays
in the document as a plain code block. The warning names the node kind
and underlines the offending markdown inside the fragment.

## Why this happens

The fragment contains one of:

- a **footnote** (`[^1]` with its `[^1]: …` definition);
- a **shortcode** (`{{{< meta key >}}}` and friends);
- CriticMarkup insertions, deletions or comments;
- a custom node produced by an extension.

## How to fix

Move the unsupported markdown out of the fragment, or build that part
with constructors instead:

- For a value from metadata, read it in Lua rather than through a
  shortcode: `meta.key` or `quarto.metadata.get("key")` inside the
  fragment as `` `{lmd} meta.key` ``.
- For a footnote, place the note in the document body rather than in the
  cell.

````markdown
```{lmd}
return {=: Version {{{< meta version >}}} here. :=}
```
````

becomes

````markdown
```{lmd}
return {=: Version `{lmd} meta.version` here. :=}
```
````

## Related errors

- A markdown *syntax* error inside a fragment is reported with the
  markdown reader's own code (for example
  [`Q-2-10`](../markdown/Q-2-10.qmd)), with a note that the error sits
  inside an lmd fragment.
- [`Q-26-3`](Q-26-3.qmd): the inline form `{=[ … ]=}` was given more than
  one block.
